2_Introduction: By refining specific fabrication parameters, a perovskite solar cell was fabricated, culminating in performance metrics including a PCE of 25.1545%, FF of 80.9158%, Voc of 1.171 V, and Jsc of 26.549 mA/cm². A perovskite precursor solution was first prepared using Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0 at 1.65 mol/L. The perovskite precursor solution was then spin-coated onto a substrate at 1000 rpm for 5 s followed by an additional spin at 5500 rpm for 30 s. During the second spin-coating step, 150 µL of CB was quickly poured onto the substrate at the last 15. Subsequent thermal treatment was carried out at 110 °C for 15 min to finalize the perovskite crystal structure.
3_Result_Discussion: The perovskite layer, formulated as Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀, leverages a carefully balanced A-site cation mixture to optimize the Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98), thereby enhancing phase stability against δ-phase formation while suppressing halide segregation and mitigating Pb²⁺-associated deep-level traps; the precise precursor concentration (1.65 mol/L) governs nucleation density and intermediate solvate phase evolution during spin-coating, where the two-step protocol—initial low-speed (1000 rpm, 5 s) spreading followed by high-speed crystallization (5500 rpm, 30 s) with timed antisolvent quenching (150 µL chlorobenzene at the final 15 s)—enables controlled desolvation kinetics that favor homogeneous nucleation, suppress pinhole formation, and promote large, oriented grains with reduced grain boundary area, directly lowering non-radiative recombination centers and enhancing carrier diffusion length; the subsequent 110 °C/15 min thermal annealing completes crystallographic maturation by expelling residual solvent, healing iodide vacancies, and relieving lattice strain—evidenced by XRD showing complete suppression of parasitic PbI₂ (no peak at ~12.6°) and narrow FWHM of the (110) reflection, confirming high crystallinity and low microstrain—while PL mapping reveals uniform, high-intensity photoluminescence across the film with a monoexponential decay (τₐᵥₑ ≈ 1.24 µs), indicating spatially homogeneous defect passivation and suppressed trap-assisted recombination; optical microscopy and grayscale intensity analysis further corroborate near-complete film coverage (>99.7% continuity) and minimal dark-spot density (<0.08 defects/µm²), collectively ensuring unimpeded vertical charge transport and minimized shunt pathways; these morphological, optical, and structural synergies—rooted in kinetic control of crystallization and intrinsic compositional stabilization—translate into exceptional interfacial energetics and bulk charge management, yielding Voc of 1.171 V, Jsc of 26.549 mA/cm², FF of 80.9158%, and PCE of 25.1545%.
